Note::capitalize¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::capitalize() const

Uppercase The First Character, Lowercase The Rest¶

capitalize() returns a new Note, same shape as the input, with each cell “sentence-cased”: the first character is uppercased in place and every following ASCII letter is lowercased. Use it to normalize a free-text field to a single leading capital — a name, a short label, a one-line description.

The transform acts on position 0 regardless of what character is there. A leading space or digit is left as-is (uppercasing a non-letter is a no-op), and the rest of the cell is lowercased from the second character on. It does not search for the first letter — "3rd place" stays "3rd place", not "3Rd place". For “capital letter at the start of every word”, use title.

The lower-casing of the tail is ASCII-only: a non-ASCII letter after position 0 is passed through unchanged. capitalize() changes case only, is idempotent, shape-preserving, and returns a fresh Note.

Example 1: A Batch¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"heLLo wORLd", "ALL CAPS", "3rd place", "café MODE"}).capitalize())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["Hello world", "All caps", "3rd place", "Café mode"]

3rd place is unchanged (position 0 is a digit); café MODE → Café mode (the é after position 0 is passed through, the ASCII tail is lowercased).

Example 2: A Scalar¶

const pluss::Note n = pluss::make_note("mIxEd").capitalize();
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"Mixed"

Example 3: A Leading Space Or Digit Is Left As-Is¶

pluss::note::print(std::cout,
                   pluss::make_note({"  spaced", "42 answers"}).capitalize())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["  spaced", "42 answers"]

Position 0 is a space / a digit; there is nothing to uppercase, and the rest is already lowercase. Chain strip first if the leading space should go.

Example 4: Shape Is Preserved¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::make_note({{"aB", "cD"}}).capitalize())
          << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1, 2], dim=2, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["Ab", "Cd"]
]

See Also¶

  • Note::title: capitalize the first letter of every word.

  • Note::upper / Note::lower: full-cell case folding.

  • Note::strip: drop a leading space before capitalizing.
